**Anatomy & Function (General Overview)** | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Structure** | • *Penile shaft*: cylindrical body made up of spongiosum tissue surrounded by tunica albuginea.
• *Glans* (“head”): rounded tip covered by mucous membrane called the foreskin when present.
• *Urethra*: tube running through the center of the shaft carrying urine and semen out of the body. | | **Blood Supply** | Arteries (e.g., dorsal artery) deliver oxygenated blood; veins drain deoxygenated blood. During arousal, increased arterial inflow causes engorgement of erectile tissues (corpora cavernosa). | | **Nerve Innervation** | Sensory nerves (pelvic plexus, pudendal nerve) transmit touch, pressure, temperature sensations. Autonomic fibers control smooth muscle relaxation/contraction during erection and ejaculation. | | **Primary Functions** | • Sexual reproduction – delivery of sperm via ejaculate into female reproductive tract.
• Urinary excretion – passage of urine from bladder to outside. | | **Developmental Stages** | • Prenatal: genital tubercle forms; differentiation guided by sex hormones.
• Puberty: surge of testosterone triggers growth, development of secondary sexual characteristics, and functional maturation. | --- ### Common Health Topics 1. **Erectile Dysfunction (ED)** - Causes: vascular issues, hormonal imbalance, neurological disorders, psychological factors, medication side effects. - Management: lifestyle changes, oral phosphodiesterase‑5 inhibitors, vacuum devices, injections, surgery, counseling. 2. **Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)** - Symptoms may include discharge, pain, sores, itching. - Prevention: condoms, regular testing, vaccination (HPV, Hepatitis B). 3. **Prostate Health** - Prostatitis, benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), prostate cancer—symptoms often involve urinary flow problems, pelvic discomfort, or abnormal bleeding. 4. **Foreskin Issues** - Circumcision status affects risk of balanitis, phimosis, or paraphimosis. Proper hygiene reduces infection risks. 5. **Surgical Interventions** - Penile prosthesis implantation for severe ED unresponsive to other treatments. - Reconstruction after trauma or congenital anomalies. --- ### When to Seek Medical Advice - Persistent difficulty achieving or maintaining erections lasting >30 minutes. - Painful urination or unusual discharge. - Unexplained swelling, redness, or lumps. - Changes in sensation or loss of feeling. - Any concerns related to fertility or sexual health. If you have specific questions or symptoms you'd like more detail on, feel free to let me know!
